jeLaime.introTexte: Twenty frank questions about what you feel for your partner today, not what you felt at the start. Some weigh more than others, because they say more. The result reads on eight levels, from the clearest to the most faded.
jeLaime.q1: Have you ever thought about leaving them?
jeLaime.q1b: Once, in a fit of anger, and it passed.
jeLaime.q2: The last "I love you" you said without being prompted:
jeLaime.q2d: I don't say it any more.
jeLaime.q3: When they rest a hand on you in passing:
jeLaime.q3a: It feels good, I move closer.
jeLaime.q3b: It leaves me neither hot nor cold.
jeLaime.q3d: I make sure it doesn't happen.
jeLaime.q4b: It has crossed my mind, like everyone.
jeLaime.q4d: I've already compared, in concrete terms.
jeLaime.q5a: I know them, they don't put me off.
jeLaime.q5d: They're all I see any more.
jeLaime.q6: An evening just the two of you, no screens, no friends:
jeLaime.q7a: I'm proud, I tell people about it.
jeLaime.q8: Your doubts about the relationship, have you confided them to anyone?
jeLaime.q8b: I've thought about it without doing it.
jeLaime.q8d: Yes, to several people, and often.
jeLaime.q9a: We make up quickly and move on.
jeLaime.q9b: They drag on more than before.
jeLaime.q9c: We don't argue any more: we don't talk any more.
jeLaime.q9d: We don't argue any more, I've nothing left to defend.
jeLaime.q10d: Gone, and I don't miss it.
jeLaime.q11: When they go away for a few days:
jeLaime.q11b: I'm fine, and glad to see them back.
jeLaime.q12: A project together, a trip, building work, a child:
jeLaime.q12a: I want that, and I'm usually the one who brings it up.
jeLaime.q13: When someone criticises them in front of you:
jeLaime.q14: Has anyone else tempted you in recent months?
jeLaime.q14b: A passing attraction, nothing came of it.
jeLaime.q14c: Something was starting, and I cut it off.
jeLaime.q15: Their small everyday gestures, the coffee made, the message during the day:
jeLaime.q15a: I notice them, and I like it.
jeLaime.q15b: I don't pay attention any more.
jeLaime.q15d: There aren't any left, and I don't ask.
jeLaime.q16: In ten years, you see yourself:
jeLaime.q16c: I don't know, the picture is blurred.
jeLaime.q17: If you found out they were seeing someone else:
jeLaime.q17b: Hurt, but I'd fight for it.
jeLaime.q18: If you're still together, it's mostly:
jeLaime.q18b: Out of attachment, out of habit.
jeLaime.q18c: For the children, the home, the money.
jeLaime.q19: The word "love" to describe what you feel:
jeLaime.q20: Starting this test, you were hoping to:
jeLaime.q20a: Reassure myself, I was afraid of finding the opposite.
jeLaime.q20b: Nothing in particular, out of curiosity.
jeLaime.q20c: Put a word on what I already feel.
jeLaime.q20d: Nothing, I already know the answer.
jeLaime.r1_t: You don't love them any more, and you knew it
jeLaime.r1_d: Your answers all point the same way, including the ones that count most: you think about leaving, you've already pictured yourself elsewhere, and the idea of them seeing someone else wouldn't do much to you. This is no longer a dip. Most people who get this result knew it before they started and mostly wanted to hear it said by someone else.
jeLaime.r1_a: You don't need one more reason. What helps now is setting a date for the conversation rather than waiting for a moment that won't come. And preparing it for them, not for you: they may know nothing of all this.
jeLaime.r2_t: What's left is no longer love
jeLaime.r2_d: Something remains, or you wouldn't be here: respect, a history, sometimes real affection. But the answers that weigh most say the wanting has gone. You no longer wait for them to come home, you no longer defend them, and you already know why you stay, and it isn't them. Staying in this state is possible for a long time, and that's precisely the risk.
jeLaime.r2_a: Ask yourself one simple thing: if nothing changes within a year, will you feel relieved or crushed? Your answer says what there is to do. If it's "relieved", the question is no longer whether you love them, it's how to tell them without damaging them.
jeLaime.r3_d: You care about this person, it shows in your answers. You wish them no harm, you're glad when things go well for them, you could still defend them. But the wanting, the missing, still choosing them: all of that has dropped a lot. It's the profile of couples who have become travelling companions, and there's no shame in it. There's only one question not to avoid: is it enough for you?
jeLaime.r3_a: Say it out loud, to yourself first: "I care about them, but I'm not in love any more". If the sentence hurts, there's still something to wake up. If it leaves you calm, you have your answer. Either way, telling them before they work it out on their own changes everything.
jeLaime.r4_d: The feeling is still there at times, but it's no longer a given, and you've started looking elsewhere, at least in your head. Your answers show gestures that no longer do anything for you, projects you dodge, an "I love you" that's become rare. Nothing is settled: at this level, couples go both ways, and what decides it is what you do in the coming months, not what you feel tonight.
jeLaime.r4_a: Do one concrete thing this week, just one: an evening together without screens, a real question about what they're going through right now, a gesture you no longer make. See what it does to you. If it does nothing, take the test again in two months: the answer will be clearer.
jeLaime.r5_d: You still love them, but on low power. Desire is less frequent, flaws irritate more, evenings together are no longer a reflex. On the other hand, the heavy answers are on the right side: you're not thinking of leaving, nobody else has taken the place, and the idea of losing them still does something to you. This is a flat stretch, not an ending. Plenty of couples go through it after a few years, a birth or a hard year.
jeLaime.r5_a: What has gone into standby comes back on with attention, not with declarations. Pick up a habit you've lost, one you had at the start and dropped without deciding to. And tell them you're going through a dip: hiding it is letting it grow.
jeLaime.r6_d: The foundation is solid: you'd still choose them, you'd be devastated to lose them, and you're not looking elsewhere. What has dropped is the energy around it: fewer gestures, fewer projects started, arguments that drag a little. That's the tiredness of a couple living their life, not a sign it's going out. The difference between the two is exactly what your answers to the important questions have just said.
jeLaime.r6_a: Don't go looking for a big reckoning, there's no call for one. Look for what tires you outside the relationship, that's often where it plays out: work, children, lack of sleep. And protect one moment together in the week, even a short one, where nobody talks logistics or money.
jeLaime.r7_t: You love them, with the normal friction
jeLaime.r7_d: Your answers describe someone in love, with the ordinary irritations of life together: a flaw that gets on your nerves, an argument that sometimes drags, an evening when you'd rather have your screen. None of it touches the foundation. You think about them when they're not there, you defend them, you picture the future together. If you took this test, it's probably because a passing doubt crossed your mind. It doesn't say much about the two of you.
jeLaime.r7_a: The doubt that brought you here still deserves a minute's look: where did it come from? A remark from someone close, tiredness, a comparison with another couple? Naming it is often enough to make it drop. And if you want to be sure, tell them you love them tonight, for no reason.
jeLaime.r8_t: You love them, and it's clear
jeLaime.r8_d: All the answers point the same way, including the ones you can't cheat on: you haven't pictured yourself elsewhere, you miss them when they're away, you'd choose them again tomorrow. The doubt that made you open this test doesn't come from your feelings. It may come from somewhere else: a stressful spell, a recent argument, a question someone asked you. But what you feel for this person is not in doubt.
jeLaime.r8_a: Keep what produces this result: noticing their gestures, wanting them, defending them. It maintains itself without effort as long as you don't take it for granted. And if the doubt comes back, take the test again in six months: that's what it's for.
